transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, what brings me in is that my head just feels really cloudy lately. I manage properties for a living, and... well, I'll just sit and stare at a board packet or an email from a vendor, and I just can't decide what to do. Even simple things that I used to handle real fast, I just get stuck on them now. It's just hard to think straight.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad. I don't feel down in the dumps or anything like that. It's really just the... the cloudiness I mentioned, and getting stuck on things. I'm not crying or feeling depressed, just frustrated that I can't do my work like I normally do.
Have you been feeling excessively worried or anxious lately?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not nervous or panicky or anything like that. I don't sit around worrying... it's just that foggy feeling I told you about. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm anxious. Just annoyed that I can't get my work done.
When did you first notice this cloudiness beginning?

It's been about two weeks. It started right around the time my husband retired and was suddenly just home all day. That's when I first noticed this... sharper change in my energy and my confidence. And then, right after that, this low, cloudy feeling just kind of set in.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy?

Yes, I have. I just haven't wanted to do much of anything. Normally, I love going to my dance class, walking around looking at the little art galleries, and cooking a big Sunday meal for my family. Those are the things that usually make me feel like myself, but lately, I just have no interest in doing any of them.
Have you noticed any change in your sleep since this started?
No, not really. I mean, I sleep about the same as I always do. I go to bed and wake up around my regular time... so, no, I haven't noticed any changes with my sleep. It's been pretty normal.
Have you been feeling more tired or less energetic than usual?

No, I wouldn't say I'm any more tired than usual. It's not really a lack of physical energy... I just, like I said, don't have the desire to do my normal activities. But my actual energy levels feel about the same as they always do.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead or of harming yourself?

Well, honestly... a few mornings lately, I've had this scary thought that maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up at all. It kind of shakes me when it happens. But I definitely don't want to hurt myself, and I don't have any kind of plan to do anything like that. It's just... a thought that crosses my mind sometimes.
Since your husband retired, have you felt sad, empty, or hopeless for most of the day on most days?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel sad or empty, really. It's just like I mentioned before, I just don't have the interest in doing things like I used to. But it's not a deep sadness or feeling hopeless all day long.
When you are away from home and not thinking about your husband’s retirement, does the cloudiness improve?

I don't think it really makes a difference, to be honest. It's just... well, I haven't noticed it getting any better when I leave the house. Even if I'm out checking on a property or just completely busy with something else, that same feeling is still there. It doesn't really seem to matter where I am or what I'm thinking about.
Have you noticed yourself forgetting things that you would normally remember, such as appointments, conversations, or important work details?
No, my memory seems to be just fine. I haven't missed any appointments or forgotten anything important with the properties. It's just the motivation to do it all that's missing, not my memory of it.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty lately?

Well, I suppose I do feel pretty guilty about work. I keep thinking... I let the residents down. I have a habit of speaking too big, you know, promising them things before I actually check the money to see if we can afford it. It just weighs on me a lot lately, even though nobody has actually come out and said I ruined anything.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite since this started?

Yeah, my eating has been a bit off lately. I mean, during the day, coffee and just a few bites of something will pretty much carry me through. And then at night... I just sort of pick at things, like tortillas or some sweets. But I'm not even really enjoying them, to be honest. I just don't have much of an appetite.
During these past two weeks, have you had little interest or pleasure in activities nearly every day?

Yes, I really have. I just... I haven't wanted to go to my dance class at all. Or go look at the little galleries like I normally do. Even cooking Sunday food for my family, I just haven't had the desire to do it lately. It's hard because... well, those are the things that usually make me feel like myself, and I just don't have any interest in them right now.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your ability to do your work or take care of your usual responsibilities?

Well, I'm still getting to work, but it's definitely harder. I've had to slow down a lot on making decisions. I actually asked my assistant to start double-checking all the vendor details for me. And... I've put off a couple of items for the board meetings, just because I really don't trust my own judgment right now. I'm doing what I have to do, but I'm just not as sharp as I need to be.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual lately?

Well, it's kind of a mix. When I'm at home, I definitely move slower... it's almost like my legs are heavy, you know? Just dragging a bit. But then, when I'm at work, especially in meetings, it's the opposite. I'll catch myself tapping my pen constantly, or shifting around in my chair. I just feel way too keyed up to sit still. So it really depends on where I am.
